title: Iron Sulphate + Regulate, Greens
last_load: Fert, Greens (100 L partial tank), Tue 27 Oct
site_check: Spray signs out on the greens, the Himalayan and the nursery. The 4th green is NOT sprayed
weather: Delta T 2–8 · wind under 15 km/h · finished before the gusts build (about 11am)
extra_checks: Bucket test: one nozzle for 1 minute at 4.1 bar
600 L/ha at 4.9 km/h needs about 3.7 L/min on 75 cm nozzle spacing (2.45 L/min on 50 cm). If it's out, call Andy before you fill
Irrigation ready to water in each green straight after it's sprayed

products.why: The label says Companion goes in first, before anything else. There's no copper in this tank, so its copper restraint is clear.

ppe_note: Iron sulphate dust stings the eyes and the mix rust-stains everything: goggles, elbow gloves and a dust mask when you tip the bags. Regulate: gloves and eye protection.
spray_rules: Greens only and skip the 4th. Then the Himalayan, and run any left over out on the nursery
Get on early: gusts build to 28–32 km/h from about 8am and 40 after midday. Spray when Delta T is 2 to 8 and stop if it's blowing off target
Water in each green straight after it's sprayed: 2–3 minutes
Keep the boom and tyres off paths and concrete, and hose off any drips straight away: iron sulphate stains
Members Guest Day is off two tees: check the start time at pre-start and stay ahead of the field. Keep people off each green until it's dry
spray_more: Proforce Regulate label: water in with 4–6 mm; not above 32 °C or on stressed, waterlogged or freshly cored turf; no DMI fungicides within 7 days; don't scarify or topdress the greens while the Poa is being regulated; no re-entry until dry. Iron sulphate SDS: keep it away from alkalis.
post_checks: Every sprayed green got its 2–3 minute water-in
Tank, boom and filters flushed twice with clean water
Iron sulphate corrodes and stains if it's left in the rig
Paths and concrete checked for drips and hosed off

flags.t: Water-in: 2–3 minutes vs the label's 4–6 mm
flags.d: Proforce Regulate's label says water in immediately with 4–6 mm of sprinkler irrigation. At the greens heads' usual 15.7 mm/hr, 2–3 minutes is about 0.5–0.8 mm (the 8th's part-circle heads run 41–68 mm/hr). The page says 2–3 minutes, as you asked.
flags.s: APVMA 88674 label · Cirrus Pro precip rates

flags.t: Wind: first light to about 8am is the window
flags.d: Open-Meteo at 2pm Tue: 13 km/h gusting 23–24 at 5–6am, 14–15 gusting 27–32 from 7 to 11am, 40+ after midday. Delta T 2.2–2.9 all morning, dry, max 16 °C.

About 12.9 kg Fe/ha (ferrous sulphate heptahydrate is 20% Fe), 6.4 g/m². A cool day (max 16 °C) keeps the blackening risk down. 80 kg in the 500 L first fill is 160 g/L, well under its 360 g/L solubility, but it needs adding slowly with the agitator running.

flags.t: Nozzles: white on 75 cm spacing adds up
flags.d: White is ISO size 08: about 3.7 L/min at 4.1 bar. At 4.9 km/h that's about 600 L/ha on 75 cm nozzle spacing, or about 900 on 50 cm. This setup and yesterday's grey-nozzle sheet both only add up on 75 cm, so the JD boom is very likely 75 cm and today's 50 cm warning was probably a false alarm. The bucket test on the rig checklist settles it.
flags.s: ISO 10625 nozzle colour code · L/ha = 600 × L/min ÷ (km/h × spacing m)

flags.d: The Regulate label says no DMI fungicides within 7 days. The last DMI on the greens on the spray pages is Evolution Advance (tebuconazole) on 19–20 Oct, 8–9 days before.

flags.t: Regulate 1.0 L/ha is in the growth-regulation range
flags.d: Label: 0.5–2 L/ha (1–2 L/ha every 4–8 weeks) for growth regulation, 2.0–2.8 L/ha for Poa suppression. 600 L/ha is inside its 400–800 L/ha water volume.
